title: Teaching video, topic to be confirmed

audience.knows: their own daily work, not yet this topic
audience.cares_about: using the idea at work without extra effort

outcome: After watching, the viewer can apply the one core idea to a situation from their own workday and pass a short check on it
through_line: One everyday workplace situation looks stuck until the core idea is seen at work, and then the same situation resolves

arc_plan.what: Open on one recognisable workplace situation or common misconception that goes wrong, shown with a cartoon colleague, not a glossary entry or agenda
arc_plan.needs: the lesson topic, and ideally a situation or misconception from the requester or the knowledge sheet

arc_plan.what: Tell the viewer, in a colleague's voice, what they will be able to do with that same situation by the end
Link the viewer's own experience of the situation to the idea, so the build feels like the next natural step
Name the core idea after it has been seen happening to the running cartoon colleague, one section per idea, each returning to the same situation
arc_plan.needs: the topic and an approved knowledge sheet with the claims to teach

arc_plan.what: Give the viewer a real decision to make in a fresh variation of the running situation, with the answer revealed afterwards, not a trivia question
Show the colleague using the idea on the original situation, as a step the viewer could copy on Monday
Return to the opening situation, now resolved, and leave one line the viewer can carry into work

must_cover.what: The single core idea of the lesson, stated plainly after it has been seen
The running workplace situation and why it goes wrong without the idea
What to do differently, as a concrete step the viewer can take

must_avoid: Opening with a formal explanation of terms or an agenda
Any 'in this video we will' phrasing
Made-up sayings presented as real words from real people
Several examples that each appear only once
A teacher's tone toward the viewer
example_posture: One running example the whole lesson returns to, taken only from the approved knowledge sheet or the requester. Invent no figures, names or case details.
visual_direction: Story-cartoon look with a person in a situation, one picture for the part that moves, a value or state that visibly changes, and a clear before and after. One loud thing at a time, with the presenter used sparingly.
voice_note: Mentor persona: a warm, capable colleague who has seen this go wrong before. Plain and direct, never lecturing.
open_questions: No topic was supplied and the knowledge sheet is empty. What is the lesson about?
Is there a specific workplace situation or misconception the requester wants as the opening?
Any look preference on how story-like, or faces versus acting? None given, so the classic way applies and the newer one can be offered later

inferred: Outcome and through-line are structural, inferred from the genre because no topic exists
Audience knows and cares_about are inferred from 'corporate employees'
Must_cover entries are placeholders pending the knowledge sheet
Hook and build marked no_material because no topic or facts exist
